about: The setup a product needs before a job starts (setup audit, 2 Nov 2026). One entry per condition. `p3 setup check` reads each one it can through gh api, or from the tranche through git, and reports it as set or missing. The proxy refuses GitHub's Actions-settings, secrets, collaborators and environments endpoints, so those conditions are confirmed once on the onboarding page and never read. `job start` runs the same check first. A condition whose `who` starts with "the developer" is the repository owner's to set; setup/DEVELOPER.md holds the steps.

conditions.what: The account sessions act as can push to the product and is not an admin of it.
conditions.why: Sessions push their own branches and open pull requests. An admin could bypass every ruleset and change settings.
conditions.who: the developer (the repository's owner): adds the session account as a collaborator and points Claude's GitHub connection at it
conditions.read: GET /user for the account, then GET /repos/{repo}: permissions.push and permissions.admin

conditions.what: An active ruleset on every branch, with nothing excluded, refuses deletion and force-push, and the session account cannot bypass it.
conditions.why: No session may delete a branch or rewrite history, on any branch (the standing safety rules).
conditions.read: GET /repos/{repo}/rulesets, then GET /repos/{repo}/rulesets/{id}: conditions.ref_name, rules, current_user_can_bypass

conditions.what: main and the tranche take changes only through a pull request, merged with a merge commit only, with the required check green; the session account cannot bypass these rules.
conditions.why: The gate is what makes a merge trustworthy; merge commits keep each pull request's history whole.
conditions.read: GET /repos/{repo}/rules/branches/{branch} for main and the tranche: pull_request.allowed_merge_methods and required_status_checks; GET /repos/{repo}/rulesets/{id}: current_user_can_bypass

conditions.what: No classic branch protection rule is on main or the tranche; the rulesets alone hold them.
conditions.why: An older classic rule was missed on 2 Nov; a classic rule adds requirements (reviews, admins exempt or not) that the rulesets and the tool do not expect, and its bypasses cannot be read by a session.
conditions.who: the developer (Settings, Branches, Branch protection rules: Delete)
conditions.read: GET /repos/{repo}/branches/{branch} for main and the tranche: protected and protection.enabled; GET /repos/{repo}/branches/{branch}/protection where readable. A rule found is reported missing, to remove

conditions.what: The repository allows merge commits, does not allow auto-merge, and does not delete a branch when its pull request merges.
conditions.why: Merges are made by the tool alone, with a merge commit; no branch is ever deleted.

conditions.what: The tranche's .claude/settings.json denies force-push, branch deletion, writing files through GitHub, and every merge route but the tool; and no rule in it blocks a session's push of its own branch.
conditions.why: The deny list holds the standing safety rules in every session; the tool's merge is the one route (Bob, 2 Nov). A rule such as Bash(git push origin :*) matches every push, so sessions could not push their own branches; each Bash rule is matched against the START's push as Claude Code matches it. Changes to the settings file itself are held by the record check, which finds any change that is not the owner's own website commit.
conditions.who: the developer, committing it on the tranche through GitHub's website; a session cannot edit its own settings file
conditions.read: the file on origin/<tranche>, through git: permissions.deny, each Bash rule matched against the push commands

conditions.what: CLAUDE.md on the tranche holds one approvals block, under the heading process/config.json names, last changed by the owner's own commit through GitHub's website.
conditions.why: A session acts on the owner's standing approvals only when CLAUDE.md holding them is on the branch it starts from (10 of 10 with it, 2 of 10 without; Bob, 2 Nov). Only the owner's own website commit may set them, so a session cannot widen its own approvals.

value.heading: process/config.json approvals.heading, default ## Standing approvals from Bob
value.last_changed_by: the owner's commit through GitHub's website

conditions.who: the developer, committing it on the tranche through GitHub's website, signed in as the owner
conditions.read: the file on origin/<tranche>, through git: the approvals headings; from the tip, following a parent whose approvals block is the same, the commit none of whose parents has its block (a shallow clone deepened first); then GET /repos/{repo}/commits/{sha}: committer web-flow, verified, author the owner (the record check's webCommitByOwner)

conditions.what: Gate artifacts (gate-row) are kept at least 90 days.
conditions.why: merge trusts a gate row only when the run's artifact still holds it (verifyRow); an expired artifact makes a green gate unprovable.
conditions.who: the developer (Settings, Actions, General: artifact and log retention); the gate workflow asks for 90 days
conditions.read: GET /repos/{repo}/actions/artifacts?name=gate-row: the newest artifact's expires_at less its created_at, in whole days; unmeasured when there is none yet

conditions.what: process/config.json on the tranche names the coordinator session.
conditions.why: Every START names the coordinator a job reports to; job start uses it when --coordinator is not given.
conditions.who: BOB, through a pull request into the tranche
conditions.read: process/config.json on origin/<tranche>, through git: coordinator

conditions.what: The checkout of the session running the check is the tranche: it descends from the tranche's tip, or it branched from a tranche commit that main does not hold and carries the tranche's current approvals block.
conditions.why: A session acts on the owner's approvals only when CLAUDE.md is on the branch it starts from (10 of 10 with it, 2 of 10 without; Bob, 2 Nov). A runner started by hand from main held no approvals and was refused session starts. job start runs this check, so a session started from the wrong branch stops with a plain message.
conditions.value: HEAD descends from origin/<tranche>; or merge-base(HEAD, origin/<tranche>) is not in origin/main and HEAD's approvals block equals the tranche's
conditions.who: BOB and every session it starts: start from the tranche
conditions.read: git in the session's own checkout: merge-base --is-ancestor origin/<tranche> HEAD; else merge-base HEAD origin/<tranche>, checked against origin/main, and the approvals block at HEAD and at origin/<tranche>

conditions.what: Every variable the product's process/config.json lists under "environment" (for example CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN and CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID) is present in the environment of the session running the check.
conditions.why: The process deploys the product so walkers can run and each round can find and fix flaws, unattended; deploy tokens in the session environment are a standard condition (Bob, 2 Nov).
conditions.value: the names in process/config.json "environment"; not configured when the config lists none
conditions.who: the developer (the Claude cloud environment's settings)
conditions.read: the environment of the session running the check: names only, never a value, a length or a prefix

conditions.what: When process/config.json names "cloudflare_account", the session's CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID is that account.
conditions.why: Deploys must reach the product's own account and no other.
conditions.value: CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID equals process/config.json cloudflare_account; not configured when the config names none
conditions.who: the developer (the Claude cloud environment's settings)
conditions.read: the environment of the session running the check: a match, yes or no; only the configured account is printed; Cloudflare's API is not called

conditions.what: The session's CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN can read, in the account process/config.json names as cloudflare_account, Workers scripts, R2 buckets, containers and Workers KV namespaces: the scopes Workers Scripts Edit, Workers R2 Storage Edit, Containers Edit and Workers KV Storage Read.
conditions.why: The product binds R2, Durable Objects, containers, service bindings, browser rendering and send_email; a token lacking Workers KV made wrangler delete exit with an error after it had succeeded (2 Nov).
conditions.who: the developer (a Cloudflare API token, saved in the Claude cloud environment's settings)
conditions.read: one harmless GET per scope on api.cloudflare.com/client/v4, the token given to curl on stdin: HTTP 200 with success true (or a bare JSON answer) is present; each scope reported present or missing; a read cannot tell Edit from Read; the token is never printed; not configured when the config names no cloudflare_account

conditions.what: Every ruleset's bypass list is empty: no app, no deploy key, no role.
conditions.why: A session can read only whether its own account may bypass a ruleset; an app, deploy key or role in the list could carry a change around the rules.
conditions.value: bypass list empty on every ruleset
conditions.read: confirmed once on the onboarding page

conditions.what: Workflows get a read-only token by default, and GitHub Actions may not create or approve pull requests.
conditions.why: Only the gate's post job is given a write token, by its own permissions block; nothing else in Actions can approve its own way into the tranche.
conditions.value: default workflow permissions: read; allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests: off
conditions.read: confirmed once on the onboarding page

conditions.what: No Actions secret is given to the process workflows; the Cloudflare and release keys live in the jobs' cloud environment only.
conditions.why: The gate runs product code from any pull request; a secret it could read would leave with that code (Bob's decision 14, 2 Nov: jobs stay in the environment that holds the keys).
conditions.value: no repository or organization Actions secret used by process-gate or process-record
conditions.read: confirmed once on the onboarding page

conditions.what: The developer is the only admin; the account sessions act as is a collaborator with Write.
conditions.why: Write lets sessions push their own branches and open pull requests; only the developer changes settings and rulesets.
conditions.value: the developer: admin; the session account: write; no one else
conditions.read: confirmed once on the onboarding page

conditions.what: No deployment environment holds a secret that a pull request run, or a branch other than main, can reach.
conditions.why: An environment's secrets would otherwise reach product code run by the gate.
conditions.value: no environments, or each one limited to main
conditions.read: confirmed once on the onboarding page
